vo: This is Luxury Intel, a weekly briefing on luxury, retail tech, jewellery and AI. Here's how it works, in two minutes.

visual.title: Luxury Intel
visual.sub: From a hundred sources to seven stories per topic, every week.

vo: Every Sunday one pipeline runs. Ingest, discover, classify, rank, build, publish. No hand-picking.
Ingestion pulls about a hundred RSS feeds and scraped pages, from WWD to JCK. A GitHub Action polls them every morning, and sites that block bots come in through Bing News.

items.p: RSS feeds and scraped pages: WWD, Vogue Business, JCK, Rapaport, Hodinkee…
GitHub Action, Mon–Sat, buffered and merged on Sunday
For outlets that block bots or have no feed

vo: Discovery fills the gaps. OpenAI writes search queries, Tavily searches the web, and the best finds join the pool.

Each article then gets one of four topics, by rules, not AI. A specialist outlet decides first, so a jewellery trade paper means jewellery. Otherwise keywords decide. No match, and the article is dropped.

visual.heading: Four topics, by rules, not AI

items.p: specialist jewellery, retail and fashion outlets set the topic
title and summary, whole-word matches for short terms
off-topic articles leave the pool (since Sep 2026)

vo: To rank, a score of source weight plus keyword and data signals minus a sponsored penalty keeps a hundred candidates per topic. The top eighteen go to GPT 4.1, which picks the final seven.

visual.heading: How seven stories get picked, per topic

rows.label: Articles in the topic this week
Kept by score: source + keywords + data signals − sponsored
Sent to GPT-4.1, max 4 per source

vo: Then the digest gets written. Summaries, Spanish and Danish translations, themes and an editor's take, all checked by a quality gate.

items.p: fails the run if something's missing

vo: The same file feeds a podcast, an AI cover image, and the Sunday email, sent with Resend to subscribers in Neon Postgres. Stripe handles paid tiers.
You can read it on the web or as an app. The site is a progressive web app, so on Android it installs to the home screen in one tap.

visual.heading: A website that installs as an app

items.p: one-tap install, runs full screen like a native app
Add to Home Screen, with a built-in guide

vo: Two market intelligence pages track twelve luxury and twelve jewellery brands. Share of voice in our coverage, three-month share prices, and company moves sorted by GPT 4.1, with a weekly summary checked against the data.

items.p: articles naming each brand, last 12 weeks
results, deals, leadership, launches, typed by GPT-4.1
short summary, every name and number checked

vo: It all runs in GitHub Actions at six a.m. UTC on Sunday. The job commits the digest to main, and every push to main deploys to Vercel.

visual.heading: Git is the database, Vercel is the stage

vo: For SEO, a daily monitor emails when something breaks, a Sunday audit tracks Search Console, bad deploys get rolled back, and a Claude agent can propose fixes as pull requests.

visual.heading: An SEO system that watches itself

items.p: emails only when something breaks or clears
opens a PR, never merges · 6 gates

vo: For AI search there's llms dot txt, a public methodology page and linked structured data, so tools like ChatGPT can cite it.

visual.heading: Built to be cited by AI search

items.p: a plain map of the site for language models
how stories are chosen, in public
one linked graph of organisation, author, articles

vo: Analytics are cookieless, with no IPs stored, and Amplitude only loads after consent.
